abstract: This study highlights the utility of shotgun metagenomics (SMg) in the diagnosis of infectious myositis, focusing on a rare case of Anncaliia algerae infection in an immunocompromised patient. This is among the first reports of SMg application in inflammatory myopathies. We conducted a monocentric prospective observational study at Pitié-Salpêtrière Hospital (2021-2024), including patients with inflammatory myopathies and suspected infectious etiologies. Diagnosis was based on clinical symptoms, paraclinical findings, myopathological examination, and SMg performed using DNA/RNA sequencing with the Illumina NextSeq 500® sequencing system and the MetaMIC® bioinformatics pipeline. Among nine patients, SMg identified A. algerae in a kidney transplant recipient with severe myositis and myocarditis. Standard microbiological techniques, including blood tests and muscle biopsy staining, failed to accurately identify the pathogen. Despite specific therapy (albendazole), the infection was fatal, underscoring the pathogen's aggressiveness in immunocompromised hosts. Other patients either recovered spontaneously or with immunosuppressants. This study demonstrates the diagnostic advantage of SMg in infectious myopathies, especially for rare pathogens like A. algerae. The unbiased nature of SMg enables pathogen identification when conventional methods fail, guiding targeted treatments. Early SMg use could improve outcomes in immunocompromised patients and warrants integration into diagnostic workflows for inflammatory myopathies. As an unbiased and culture-free pan-pathogenic method, SMg enables the identification of pathogens, including unexpected ones, and can be used in addition to routine procedures for inflammatory myopathy diagnosis.
